light.label: Medium to bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates low light, but needs more than the green forms to stay this pale

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep out of direct sun

snap: A compact Aglaonema whose long, pointed leaves are almost entirely creamy white, edged and flecked in green. It is the palest of the group and the most light-hungry, but it still keeps its colour well away from a window. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Aglaonemas come from the shaded forest floors of tropical Asia, from India through Southeast Asia to southern China. Super White is a cultivated selection bred for the white in its leaves. It is clumping rather than climbing: new stems rise from the base and the plant slowly thickens into a bushy mound, staying close to a foot or two tall.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top two inches of the mix have dried, in a loose, well-draining mix. Keep it warm: below roughly 15°C the leaves curl and brown, and a draught from an air-conditioner or an open window in winter does it in a night. Direct sun is the other thing to avoid — the white has little chlorophyll to protect it, so it scorches faster than any green Aglaonema.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: With so little green in each leaf, it makes less food than its darker relatives and grows slowly — which suits a desk, since it stays the size you bought for a long time. The trade-off is that it wants more light than they do. In a dim corner the new leaves come in greener and the white slips away, which is the plant adjusting rather than anything you have done wrong; moving it brighter brings the pale leaves back.
